assertions.name: log_normaliser_A_exponent
assertions.source: log-log slope of log Z(3A) over A=2..64 vs the SEMF volume-term exponent

description: ROAST-M2 exponent-only test of the A-nucleons -> 3A-strands map: does the framework reproduce the extensive (A^1) exponent with magnitude free?

discriminating_power.note: Measured 1.674 on A=2..64 and rising to 1.995 on A=1024..4096 -- asymptotically 2, approached slowly because of the linear term. Either way it is NOT 1, so the exponent test does discriminate between the corpus's actual normaliser and a plausible alternative, and would also detect an affine strand rule n = 3A + c, c != 0. The test is therefore not vacuous.

data.verdict: EXPONENT TEST PASSES. The 3-strands-per-nucleon map yields a normaliser whose logarithm is exactly linear in A -- the SEMF volume term's exponent -- with the coefficient constant to all computed digits. This is a NEGATIVE for the ROAST's R2 hypothesis that the braid->nucleus map is the defective step: the map's A-scaling is right. The residual is a pure multiplicative constant, not a shape error. Deliberately not matched to any structural candidate (see module docstring).
